lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the shared Campanulaceae framework—fused corolla, inferior ovary, 5-part flowers and secondary pollen presentation—then split the project into a Triodanis free-stamen/pore-capsule door and a Lobelia anther-tube/bilabiate door.

project_scope.selection_mode: Project module across Triodanis and Lobelia
project_scope.note: Six source rows represent five species-level concepts plus one accepted infraspecific concept: source Triodanis biflora is currently treated by Kew as Triodanis perfoliata subsp. biflora.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Find a single flower—not a composite head—and inspect the ovary position. In the project genera the corolla is fused and the ovary is inferior, with the other flower parts arising above it.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Mostly herbs in the project pool, with simple alternate leaves. Milky latex is common in Campanulaceae but is not needed as a crew field test.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers usually 5-merous with a sympetalous corolla and an inferior ovary containing many ovules. Five stamens are present, but their relationship differs sharply by project genus: free in Triodanis, anthers connate into a tube around the style in Lobelia.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Capsule with many seeds in the project taxa. Triodanis capsules open by pores in the lower portion; Lobelia cardinalis has an apically valvate capsule.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: First confirm individual fused-corolla flowers over an inferior ovary. Then ask: regular/star-like with free stamens = Triodanis; strongly bilabiate with an anther tube = Lobelia.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: individual flower → alternate leaves → calyx/flower attachment → closed flower → Lobelia contrast → inferior ovary → capsule pore → anther tube and plunger
visual_lesson.intro: Campanulaceae is the bellflower family, but not every bellflower is shaped like a bell. Compare purple, near-regular Triodanis flowers with red, two-lipped Lobelia flowers. Both use one individual fused corolla and an inferior ovary, not an Asteraceae flower head. Photos below name exactly which structure is visible; missing microscopes and capsules remain honest placeholders.

steps.title: 1 · One flower with five corolla lobes
steps.photo_role: individual flower front / five fused-corolla lobes
steps.look_for: One violet star-like flower; count five lobes and notice the pale center. This is ONE flower, not a composite Asteraceae head.
steps.why_it_matters: A good first doorway into the Campanulaceae flower pattern. This photograph does not show a dissected ovary.

steps.title: 2 · Follow alternate leaves to the stem
steps.look_for: On the flowering stem, the green alternate leaves attach at successive nodes. Some upper leaf bases partly clasp the stem; confirm the entire base.
steps.why_it_matters: Leaf attachment is a practical field clue in Triodanis, but not every Campanulaceae species has clasping leaves.

steps.title: 3 · Flower attachment and green calyx
steps.look_for: At the leaf axils, examine purple corolla lobes and the green support/calyx beneath. We need a true cutaway to identify the inferior ovary boundary confidently.
steps.why_it_matters: Connects the flower to the stem without making an unverified ovary-arrow claim.

steps.title: 4 · See a closed self-pollinating flower
steps.look_for: The little closed floral structure near a node is a cleistogamous flower; this lower-resolution reference can be enlarged, but is not an anatomy dissection.
steps.why_it_matters: Some bellflower relatives make inconspicuous self-pollinating flowers alongside showier open blooms.

steps.title: 5 · Meet Lobelia's very different flower
steps.image_alt: Red cardinal flower (Lobelia cardinalis), Campanulaceae flower-shape reference
steps.look_for: Observe the red, strongly asymmetric flower with upper and lower lobes. This is a labeled external reference, NOT an installed photo of Triodanis nor a confirmed anther-tube dissection.
steps.why_it_matters: The family contains both near-radial Triodanis and two-lipped Lobelia: do not define Campanulaceae by flower color or symmetry alone.

steps.title: 6 · Locate the inferior ovary
steps.photo_role: inferior ovary flower side and cutaway
steps.look_for: The ovary lies below the place where the calyx, petals and stamens attach. Need a real macro or cutaway that actually reveals that connection.
steps.why_it_matters: A major Campanulaceae reproductive clue; cannot accurately infer location from the available front flower photographs.

steps.title: 7 · Find the little seed-release window
steps.look_for: Turn a fully ripe capsule to the side and find the real small opening. Its position helps distinguish perfoliata from biflora. An exact pore macro with ruler is not yet installed.
steps.why_it_matters: Capsule dehiscence separates look-alikes even after blossoms disappear.

steps.title: 8 · Check Lobelia's anther tube and pollen plunger
steps.photo_role: Lobelia stamens / joined anthers / style phases macro
steps.look_for: Five anthers join around the style and present pollen before the stigma extends. The flower-shape reference above does not show the detailed mechanism; microscope photos are needed.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates Lobelia's reproductive architecture from Triodanis free stamens.

comparisons.title: Campanulaceae vs Asteraceae
comparisons.rule: Both are Asterales and commonly have inferior ovaries plus secondary pollen presentation. Campanulaceae project flowers are individual fused-corolla flowers producing many-seeded capsules; Asteraceae packs many tiny florets into a capitulum and each floret usually makes a one-seeded cypsela.

comparisons.title: Triodanis vs Lobelia
comparisons.rule: Triodanis = more regular 5-lobed flower, free stamens, lower-axil cleistogamous flowers and a pore-opening capsule. Lobelia = strongly zygomorphic 2+3 corolla, connate anther tube around the style and an apically valvate capsule.

visual_lesson.caveat: The genus shares Campanulaceae traits but its photo roles cannot stand in for all family members. The Lobelia photo is an EXTERNAL licensed reference, not an installed local specimen. No real arrow or pore detection has been verified.

prior_steps_before_photo_polish.title: 1 · Locate the inferior ovary
prior_steps_before_photo_polish.look_for: The corolla, calyx and stamens arise above the ovary; the ovary is embedded below the visible flower.
prior_steps_before_photo_polish.why_it_matters: This is a strong family-level Asterales character shared by both project genera.

prior_steps_before_photo_polish.title: 2 · Triodanis door: regular flower + free stamens
prior_steps_before_photo_polish.photo_role: Triodanis flower face and opened flower
prior_steps_before_photo_polish.look_for: A blue-purple rotate to shallowly campanulate flower usually divided into 5 lobes, with 5 stamens free from one another; lower axils may also contain tiny cleistogamous flowers.
prior_steps_before_photo_polish.why_it_matters: Separates Venus's-looking-glass from Lobelia without relying on color.

prior_steps_before_photo_polish.title: 3 · Find the Triodanis pore-opening capsule
prior_steps_before_photo_polish.look_for: An elongated inferior capsule opening through 2–3 pores in the lower part of the fruit.
prior_steps_before_photo_polish.why_it_matters: A highly memorable genus-level fruit character after the showy corolla is gone.

prior_steps_before_photo_polish.title: 4 · Lobelia door: split two-lipped corolla
prior_steps_before_photo_polish.look_for: The corolla is split nearly to the base dorsally and forms a bilabiate limb: 2 upper lobes and 3 lower lobes.
prior_steps_before_photo_polish.why_it_matters: Explains why cardinal flower looks so different from Triodanis while remaining in the same family.

prior_steps_before_photo_polish.title: 5 · Find the Lobelia anther tube
prior_steps_before_photo_polish.look_for: Five anthers joined into a tube around the style; the reproductive column projects through the dorsal corolla split.
prior_steps_before_photo_polish.why_it_matters: This is the key Lobelia mechanism and a major contrast with free-stamen Triodanis.

prior_steps_before_photo_polish.title: 6 · Show plunger pollen presentation
prior_steps_before_photo_polish.look_for: The style pushes pollen through the anther tube, then the receptive 2-lobed stigma emerges later.
prior_steps_before_photo_polish.why_it_matters: Turns an abstract Asterales pollen-presentation concept into a visible sequence.

prior_steps_before_photo_polish.title: 7 · Clean up Triodanis biflora
prior_steps_before_photo_polish.look_for: Source Triodanis biflora → accepted Triodanis perfoliata subsp. biflora under current Kew.
prior_steps_before_photo_polish.why_it_matters: Avoids counting the subspecies as a separate species while preserving the familiar source name.
